walkthroughs.body_html:
Statistical Distributions — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Statistical Distributions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Statistical Distributions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Probability density function”?
options: E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.
PDF f(x) for continuous X. P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx. Total area under curve = 1.

PMF p(x) gives P(X = x) for discrete X. Σp(x) = 1. Used to define distribution.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Linear combinations”?
options: E(X) = Σx·p(x) (discrete) or ∫x·f(x) dx (continuous). Long-run average value.
Var(X) = E(X²) − [E(X)]². Spread of distribution. SD = √Var(X).
Discrete: countable outcomes (binomial, Poisson). Continuous: any value in an interval (normal, exponential).
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b; Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). For independent X, Y: Var(X+Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y).
